newsitem.title: UK: Battered gold dips below psychological $350 level.
newsitem.headline: Battered gold dips below psychological $350 level.

text.p: The price of gold sank to $350 an ounce on Wednesday, hitting a key psychological signpost along its steep downward path.
Badly battered by a surging dollar and stock markets, and under pressure from fresh selling, gold slid to $349.50/$349.90 an ounce in early trading.
Prices anxiously straddled either side of that key level as bullion was fixed at $350.10 an ounce, the lowest fixing since September 15, 1993.
But bullion dealers and analysts said it was unlikely to find much support there for long.
"It's looking very weak," a London bullion dealer said, noting that some market players had forced the market lower in early trading by borrowing gold to sell on the spot market.
"At this level people are expecting New York to come in and sell it lower," he added.
Gold prices have been sliding steadily lower to levels not seen for more than three years since hitting a high of $417 an ounce in February 1996.
Investors have ignored gold in favour of strong equities markets, while physical buyers have sat back waiting for prices to bottom out.
Meanwhile, market sentiment has become increasingly bearish as fears grow that European central banks will sell their gold reserves ahead of European Monetary Union.
Tuesday's upbeat remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan spelled more bad news for bullion as the dollar soared against the mark and yen, further encouraging holders of gold to sell.
European stock markets also shot to record highs on Wednesday on the back of Greenspan's speech and Wall Street's strong performance on Tuesday.
Gold was unlikely to have bottomed out at $350, technical analysts said, with $345 an ounce tapped as the nearest support level.
"That is quite a good retracement level and the intersection of a long-term trend," said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
But eventually gold may even test the waters at $330, the significant low level from 1993, some analysts said.
The other precious metals have eased in sympathy with gold and remained vulnerable to the downside, analysts said.
Silver has remained relatively resilient during gold's drop but was moderately lower at $4.68/$4.70, down four cents from Tuesday's London close.
Platinum, like gold trading at 3-1/4 year lows, was down $3.00 at $355.75/$356.75.
Its sister metal palladium was little changed at $120.75/$121.75 an ounce.
